key_insight: For linear elliptic Dirichlet PDEs, neural approximation power alone does not guarantee PINN convergence: discrete stability and accurate comparison networks within admissible trial classes are also needed.
engineering_relevance: The framework guides collocation-point counts and scale-dependent, physics-balanced boundary weighting so sampled residual losses can control solution error.
method: Extend kernel collocation theory using elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency.
Identify stable admissible neural subclasses and quantify their sampling requirements.
Construct admissible tanh-MLP comparison networks to prove constrained convergence and conditional unconstrained convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence results for tanh-MLPs, but no numerical benchmarks or empirical error measurements.
watch_item: Unconstrained PINN convergence remains conditional under joint network and sampling refinement; generic approximation guarantees alone are insufficient.
paper_title: Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
